title: Baseline zero-angle drag
note: All surfaces have zero roughness; all-turbulent flow is selected. Direct installed-engine curves, without correction.

title: Transonic drag detail
note: The denser transonic comparison tests the location, width and magnitude of the drag rise, rather than matching one peak.

title: Drag residuals by Mach
note: Positive residual means RASAero predicts more drag. The sign and size vary with geometry and Mach.

title: Nose shapes at L/D = 1.5
note: Finless 4 in body, overall length 60 in, nose length 6 in. Body length changes to hold total length fixed.

title: Nose shapes at L/D = 3
note: Finless 4 in body, overall length 60 in, nose length 12 in. Body length changes to hold total length fixed.

title: Nose shapes at L/D = 4.5
note: Finless 4 in body, overall length 60 in, nose length 18 in. Body length changes to hold total length fixed.

title: Tangent-ogive fineness sweep
note: Nose length changes at fixed overall length. L/D is nose length divided by body diameter.

title: Sensitivity to shortening the nose
note: The finite difference contains both the nose-shape change and the associated body wetted-area change. Both solvers receive the same dimensions.

title: Nose-shape transonic detail at L/D = 3
note: Geometry and zero roughness are matched. Different onset, peak Mach and width of the transonic rise remain even in shapes that agree closely at Mach 2.

title: Body length and fin count controls
note: The first three panels vary only finless-body length. The fourth checks the 3-fin count against the original 4-fin family.

title: Square fin thickness sweep
note: Fixed planform and sweep. The 0.001 in case is an asymptotic diagnostic, not a representative hardware design.

title: Beveled fin thickness sweep
note: Fixed planform and sweep. The 0.001 in case is an asymptotic diagnostic, not a representative hardware design.

title: Leading bevel length sweep
note: FX1 is measured parallel to the body. Maximum thickness is 0.125 in and the trailing edge remains blunt.

title: Square fin sweep
note: Root/tip chords, span and thickness are fixed. Leading-edge sweep distance varies without fin overhang past the body.

title: Beveled fin sweep
note: Root/tip chords, span and thickness are fixed. Leading-edge sweep distance varies without fin overhang past the body.

title: Fin span and aspect ratio
note: Root/tip chords, sweep and thickness are fixed. Each solver uses the same exposed fin span.

title: Fin taper at fixed sweep
note: Sweep is 2 in for all four cases; compare with the corresponding 2 in-sweep baseline, whose tip chord is 2 in.

title: Net drag added by fins
note: Finned-minus-finless subtraction includes fin/body interference and changes in exposed body surface. It is not an isolated RASAero fin-pressure coefficient.

title: Thin-profile limits and rounded control
note: These limits test whether the models approach a consistent finite-planform, vanishing-thickness behavior.

title: Geometric scale and Reynolds number
note: Every external length is scaled together; reference area follows diameter squared. At common Mach and atmosphere, dimensionless geometry is unchanged and Reynolds number varies.

title: Fin drag versus upstream body length
note: Only the cylindrical body length changes. Net fin additions expose the influence of the skin-friction reference length.

title: Physical roughness: Hbody
note: Gray: native OR nearest available finish (2, 5, 20, 150 micrometers respectively). Blue: native OR correlation reconstructed at the exact RAS roughness, verified against all native finish curves; no OR application changes.

title: Physical roughness: Hsq
note: Gray: native OR nearest available finish (2, 5, 20, 150 micrometers respectively). Blue: native OR correlation reconstructed at the exact RAS roughness, verified against all native finish curves; no OR application changes.

title: Physical roughness: Hbev
note: Gray: native OR nearest available finish (2, 5, 20, 150 micrometers respectively). Blue: native OR correlation reconstructed at the exact RAS roughness, verified against all native finish curves; no OR application changes.

title: Roughness-induced drag at fixed Mach
note: Numerical physical roughness is matched in the reconstructed OR correlation. Pressure and base terms retain their native OR values.

title: Isolated fin response to physical roughness
note: Two subtractions remove smooth baseline drag and the finless-body roughness response. RASAero square-fin curves remain at zero to floating-point precision; beveled fins respond. OR exact-roughness curves are reconstructed from its native correlation.

title: Laminar-to-turbulent option: finned rockets
note: OR perfectFinish=true and RAS All Turbulent Flow=false. These settings enable the respective transition models; their transition equations are not assumed identical.

title: Sensitivity to flow-transition treatment
note: Subtracting the fully turbulent baseline separates the change due to each program's flow option from the baseline pressure-drag disagreement.

title: Isolated fin response to flow transition
note: Subtract the body-only response to the flow option from the finned-rocket response. This isolates the net fin dependency without labeling it as a proprietary RASAero internal pressure or friction term.

title: Nozzle-area sensitivity: Hbody
note: Aero-only probes. OR has no corresponding nozzle-area correction here; its baseline is shown to reveal the missing dependency, not as a matched powered-flow prediction.

title: Nozzle-area sensitivity: Hsq
note: Aero-only probes. OR has no corresponding nozzle-area correction here; its baseline is shown to reveal the missing dependency, not as a matched powered-flow prediction.

title: Test of nozzle-area scaling
note: The dashed line uses the observed full-area value. It tests area proportionality; it does not identify the absolute body-base coefficient.

title: Wind-axis drag at 0, 2 and 4 degrees
note: Body-axis forces are compared directly. Wind-axis drag/lift use CD=CA cos(alpha)+CN sin(alpha), CL=CN cos(alpha)-CA sin(alpha). RAS lift is reconstructed for power-off; its raw CL column corresponds to power-on when nozzle area is nonzero.

title: Axial force at 0, 2 and 4 degrees
note: Body-axis forces are compared directly. Wind-axis drag/lift use CD=CA cos(alpha)+CN sin(alpha), CL=CN cos(alpha)-CA sin(alpha). RAS lift is reconstructed for power-off; its raw CL column corresponds to power-on when nozzle area is nonzero.

title: Normal force at 0, 2 and 4 degrees
note: Body-axis forces are compared directly. Wind-axis drag/lift use CD=CA cos(alpha)+CN sin(alpha), CL=CN cos(alpha)-CA sin(alpha). RAS lift is reconstructed for power-off; its raw CL column corresponds to power-on when nozzle area is nonzero.

title: Wind-axis lift at 0, 2 and 4 degrees
note: Body-axis forces are compared directly. Wind-axis drag/lift use CD=CA cos(alpha)+CN sin(alpha), CL=CN cos(alpha)-CA sin(alpha). RAS lift is reconstructed for power-off; its raw CL column corresponds to power-on when nozzle area is nonzero.

title: Center of pressure at 0 degrees
note: CP is measured from the nose tip in body diameters; this is not a stability margin. OR warns of limitations of its body-force treatment above Mach 1.1.

title: Center of pressure at 4 degrees
note: CP is measured from the nose tip in body diameters; this is not a stability margin. OR warns of limitations of its body-force treatment above Mach 1.1.

title: Normal-force slope over 0 to 4 degrees
note: Both plotted slopes use the same 0-to-4-degree secant definition; neither is assumed to be the infinitesimal derivative in nonlinear flow.

title: Rogers Modified Barrowman: CN at 4 degrees
note: Default and modified RAS settings share geometry and drag-flow inputs. This isolates the normal-force/body-interference option, compared with unmodified MIT OR.

title: Rogers Modified Barrowman: CP at 4 degrees
note: Default and modified RAS settings share geometry and drag-flow inputs. This isolates the normal-force/body-interference option, compared with unmodified MIT OR.

title: Rogers Modified Barrowman: CD at 4 degrees
note: Default and modified RAS settings share geometry and drag-flow inputs. This isolates the normal-force/body-interference option, compared with unmodified MIT OR.
